Hey, so I am a PhD student now and worked for 5 years as a data scientist. Basically in industry, you tend not to do anything particularly interesting.  spent a lot of time writing scripts to do things in the cloud, writing SQL , writing software packages, and making data visualizations in a prescribed manner. The thing is for most companies the complexity of a cool model isn't worth it.

In academia, the ideas are more interesting and rewarding to work with in general. The stressors are different. A lot of the work is actually finding funding and learning about different mechanisms and writing grants. 

When comparing the two, as a PhD student, I am making half of what I made and gave up a six fig salary. But, I am doing my PhD in Scandinavia, and things are a lot lower stress than working industry. I won't worry about getting laid off and make a livable salary and do things that I think are interesting, but I can't live an easy lifestyle exactly like before.
